name: Faith
label: Dischord
lede: Two years, one side of an LP and an eight-song EP, and the band a lot of D.C. kids felt closer to than Minor Threat.

eras.title: Filling the quiet
eras.text: By fall 1981 several D.C. bands had broken up at once, Minor Threat briefly among them, and the scene went quiet. SOA veterans Michael Hampton and Ivor Hanson, Untouchables singer Alec MacKaye and Wilson High bassist Chris Bald formed Faith, and within weeks of their first show they were opening for Bad Brains at CBGB.

years.h: Faith forms out of SOA and the Untouchables
years.p: [[Michael Hampton|4ed83c42-6348-4368-903e-9116bfa49b8e]] and [[Ivor Hanson|a17981f7-ab3d-46dc-859a-582ac894cb20]] come over from [[SOA|e54cb250-3502-4c32-9482-70488bd9a8cb]], [[Alec MacKaye|bb05a948-ea44-4c9b-9d19-2a48f757ca22]] from the Untouchables, and fellow Wilson High kid [[Chris Bald|0838359b-95a7-48e9-a9f6-0e8f40bb34d2]] picks up the bass. Alec is [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]]'s younger brother.

years.cap: Alec MacKaye and Michael Hampton at the Chancery, Washington, D.C., 1981.
years.h: Faith's first show: H.B. Woodlawn High School, Arlington
years.p: Faith debut at H.B. Woodlawn High School in Arlington. Before the year is out they're also playing the Chancery in D.C.

years.cap: Recorded at CBGB, December 1981, and released later by Outer Battery.
years.p: A few weeks after their first show, Faith are at CBGB in New York opening for Bad Brains. Someone rolls tape, and the set later comes out as Live at CBGB's on Outer Battery.

eras.title: Their side of the record
eras.text: Faith spent 1982 getting onto vinyl and getting bigger. Dischord paired them with Void for the split LP Faith/Void, and Faith's sound was already starting to change.

years.p: Twelve Faith songs on one side, [[Void|960a1d2f-2b5f-4fcf-bf11-4957529a6508]] on the other, recorded at Inner Ear; the sleeve credits production to Ian, Jeff, Don, Bert and the band. According to Wikipedia, the first pressing sold out in two weeks.
years.xp:
The Washington Post later described Faith as taking the snarl of British punk, speeding it up and making it distinctly American. Next to Void's chaotic side, the Faith side is taut and pointed.

The record found fans far from D.C. Kurt Cobain put Faith/Void in his top 50 albums of all time, and Thurston Moore called it the most potent distillation of early D.C. straight edge hardcore.

years.h: Live at the Wilson Center, April 4, 1982
yt: Live at the Wilson Center, April 4, 1982

eras.title: Stopping at the top
eras.text: Early in 1983 guitarist Eddie Janney made Faith a five-piece, and the band wrote longer, more thoughtful songs. Then they decided they were done. Their last record, Subject to Change, came out after their last show, which is part of why it hit people so hard.

years.h: Eddie Janney joins Faith on second guitar
years.p: [[Eddie Janney|323dd1dd-23e4-45ce-9aa9-c5492096d604]], Alec MacKaye's old Untouchables bandmate, joins alongside guitarist Michael Hampton. Faith are now a five-piece.

q: It was a good time to stop.
years.src: Washington City Paper · Dischord Records · Wikipedia
years.p: Faith play their final show as headliners, about two years after their November 1981 debut. The fans weren't ready for the band to end.
years.xp:
No single reason for Faith's split is on the record. Michael Hampton, looking back decades later, simply thought the timing was right.

The audience felt otherwise. Dischord's own bio says that while [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] gets held up as the defining D.C. band of those years, for many people who lived there it was Faith they connected with most. [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] remembered how unhappy people were.

years.src: Dischord Records · Wikipedia · Washington City Paper
years.p: Eight songs, about thirteen minutes, on a 12-inch EP produced by [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and Faith at Inner Ear. It comes out roughly four months after the August 1983 last show, so most listeners meet the five-piece Faith after it's gone.
years.xp:
Subject to Change is the only record of the five-piece Faith, with Eddie Janney's guitar alongside Michael Hampton's.

The fans who missed that lineup live took the record hard. [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] summed up the reaction years later.

eras.title: Everybody starts the next band
eras.text: Faith's five members fanned out across the next wave of D.C. music. Follow almost any branch of mid-80s Dischord back far enough and you hit one of them.

years.p: Former Faith guitarist Eddie Janney co-founds Rites of Spring with [[Guy Picciotto|f8200cea-b5e9-4145-b5a5-1d0838f2c288]], part of the wave that follows hardcore in D.C.

years.h: Three Faith members and Ian MacKaye form [[Embrace|9d1ad8e3-8740-429a-bdc5-52f96a9c4431]]
years.p: Michael Hampton, Chris Bald and Ivor Hanson back [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]], who has moved on from [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]]. The older brother ends up singing in front of his younger brother Alec's old band.

years.h: Eddie Janney and Michael Hampton form One Last Wish
years.p: The two Faith guitarists reunite in [[One Last Wish|94f18045-7fe2-41df-bf24-0bed21c88eb8]], which later becomes [[Happy Go Licky|4c18be5e-2e53-41a4-a4a1-d9080ff88f8c]]. Alec MacKaye and Chris Bald, meanwhile, go on to form [[Ignition|3cb2b7d6-1f0b-4ac5-b67f-52132f3d3b61]].

years.h: Michael Hampton and Ivor Hanson again, in Manifesto
years.p: Hampton and Hanson, who played together in SOA, Faith and Embrace, team up once more in the band Manifesto, ten years after SOA.

eras.title: Renewed Faith
eras.text: Nearly thirty years on, Dischord went back to Faith's tapes. The 2011 reissue Subject to Change plus First Demo put the band's first recordings next to its last and sent a new round of writers back to Faith/Void.

years.h: Faith on the box set 20 Years of Dischord
years.p: Faith take their place on Dischord's 20th-anniversary box set.

years.h: Faith's 1981 demo finally comes out, with Subject to Change
years.p: Faith's eleven-song December 1981 demo, produced by [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] at Inner Ear, stayed unreleased for 30 years. Dischord paired it with the remastered Subject to Change as No. 172.
years.xp:
Nearly every song on the demo had been re-recorded for Faith/Void in 1982, so the tape sat on the shelf.

The 2011 edition was remastered from the original tapes and was the EP's first time on vinyl since 1988, this time on clear vinyl.
play: Subject to Change plus First Demo

years.h: Craig Finn calls Faith/Void one of the most vital hardcore records
years.p: In The Guardian, [[The Hold Steady|4883523d-fc0e-4d0d-802c-91379e767083]]'s Craig Finn calls the 1982 split LP Faith/Void one of the most vital hardcore records ever released.
